name: Jabal Amil Frontier
inspired_by: Southern Lebanon between the Litani river and the Blue Line, as of 2026: a narrow coastal plain of citrus and banana groves, terraced limestone hills with dense hilltop villages, the deep Litani gorge, and a heavily damaged border strip. UNIFIL is in its final mandate year (drawdown through 2026) and Israeli forces hold much of the south after March 2026. All towns are fictional.
climate: Mediterranean (Koppen Csa). Hot dry summers (30-34 C on the coast, cooler in the hills), mild wet winters (10-16 C) with 600-900 mm of rain from November to March; frost and occasional snow above 700 m.
seasons: Winter (Dec-Feb): heavy rain fronts, low cloud on the ridges, muddy terraces, swollen Litani
Spring (Mar-May): green terraces, tobacco planting, wildflowers, clear air
Summer (Jun-Sep): dry and hot, brush fires on the hillsides, haze over the coast
Autumn (Oct-Nov): olive harvest, first rains, tobacco leaves drying on strings

vegetation: date and fan palms on the shore
sand dune scrub with sea daffodil
sage and thyme garrigue on bare limestone
willows and oleander along the river
fig and wild vine on the cliffs

terrain.relief: Steep and broken. A 1-3 km coastal plain rises abruptly into limestone hills cut by deep east-west wadis; ridges and hilltops at 500-880 m carry villages; the Litani cuts a 200-400 m deep gorge across the north of the map before turning west to the sea.
features: Litani gorge with a few bridges and fords
a crusader-era castle ruin on a spur
border fence, patrol road and concrete wall sections on the south edge
terrain.water: The Litani (15-30 m wide, perennial, with a small dam upstream at the north-east edge); seasonal streams in the wadis; village springs and cisterns; the sea along the west edge with a small harbour.

generator.approach: Heightmap at 5-10 m resolution. Base coastal ramp (0 m at the shore rising east), plus ridged noise for the hill mass, then carve the Litani as a deep spline canyon and wadis by flow accumulation. Terraces are a post-pass: on terraced_hills slopes of 8-30 degrees, quantise height into 1.5-2.5 m steps with a stone-wall edge flag for the structure layer.

noise_layers.purpose: coast-to-ridge rise and broad ridge massifs
east-west ridges and spurs between wadis
karst dolines and sinkholes on ridge tops

generator.erosion: Hydraulic erosion (60 iterations) to sharpen wadis; thermal erosion capped at 45 degrees leaves limestone cliffs in the gorge.
generator.rivers: Litani as a hand-placed spline across the north third, canyon depth 200-400 m, floor 30-80 m wide; wadis follow flow accumulation to the sea or the Litani.
generator.settlement_flattening: Villages seed on knolls and ridge saddles; flatten per building plot (not whole village) so streets climb with the slope; coastal town core flattened to a 5 m bench.
generator.notes: Short sightlines between ridges (1-3 km) and long ones across the gorge. Bridges over the Litani (3) and the coastal highway are the convoy chokepoints. Caves are POI-stamped volumes for the structure layer, not generated by noise.

settlements.architecture: Dense hilltop villages of two- to four-storey reinforced-concrete houses with cinder-block infill, many built with emigrant money: arched balconies, stone cladding on the facade, flat roofs with water tanks, solar heaters and rebar stubs. A domed mosque or a church with a bell tower, a husseiniya hall, a municipal building, a school. Many houses in the border-side villages are damaged or destroyed.
settlements.footprint_m: house 12x14 to 16x20; plots 20x30 with garden walls
settlements.wall_class: Concrete frame and slabs thick (cover); cinder-block infill 15-20 cm thin (breachable); stone-clad facades medium; garden walls 30 cm stone thick.
layout_rules: organic streets following contours, 1-2 main roads along the ridge
village square with mosque or church, shops and a municipal building
rubble lots and collapsed buildings: 10-40% in border-side villages
only 2-3 vehicle approaches; footpaths on terraces

settlements.architecture: Coastal market town with four- to eight-storey concrete apartment blocks, ground-floor shops, an old stone quarter with vaulted souq lanes and courtyard houses, a fishing harbour and a corniche. Rooftop clutter: water tanks, antennas, solar panels.
settlements.wall_class: Apartment frames thick; infill thin; old stone quarter 60-80 cm limestone walls thick and vaulted.
layout_rules: grid of newer blocks around an organic old core
corniche and harbour on the west edge
main road north-south on the coastal highway
market street and a large mosque near the old quarter
Palestinian-refugee-camp-style dense quarter on the edge (narrow alleys, 3-5 storeys)

settlements.architecture: Farmhouses among orchards: one or two storeys, flat roof, a packing shed, greenhouses on the coast, tobacco drying frames in the hills.
settlements.wall_class: Houses cinder block thin to medium; greenhouses no cover.
layout_rules: scattered in orchards on the plain and terraces
track access from the nearest village

settlements.architecture: Military positions: hilltop outposts of the occupying force (earth berms, concrete T-walls, observation masts); UN positions (prefab cabins, HESCO, white-painted towers, blue flags); army barracks; and dug-in positions in the maquis with bunkers and cave entrances.
settlements.footprint_m: UN post 80x120; hilltop outpost 150x200; bunker entrance 3x3
settlements.wall_class: HESCO, T-walls and berms thick; prefabs thin; bunkers and caves effectively indestructible.
layout_rules: on hilltops and spurs with long views
UN posts marked white with blue signage
bunker and cave entrances hidden in maquis and terrace walls

infrastructure.roads: A four-lane coastal highway on the plain, two-lane ridge roads linking villages, steep switchbacks into wadis, and agricultural tracks along terraces. Three bridges over the Litani (one destroyed, one temporary) and the coastal highway bridge are chokepoints. The border patrol road runs along the south edge.
infrastructure.rail: None (a disused coastal line bed only).
infrastructure.power: Overhead lines on wooden and steel poles, frequent outages, private diesel generators in every neighbourhood, rooftop solar.
infrastructure.ports: Small fishing and commercial harbour at the coastal town; the LHD stands off the coast.
infrastructure.airfields: None. A helipad at the UN headquarters compound on the coast.
infrastructure.checkpoints: Occupying-force checkpoints at road junctions in the south; Lebanese army checkpoints north of the Litani (no faction file: neutral NPCs); UN posts along the patrol road; earth berms closing village entrances near the border.

pois.contract_use: recover a downed drone nearby; escort an aid convoy through its control zone (neutral client)

conditions: winter storm fronts with heavy rain
low cloud and fog on ridges
weather.visibility_notes: Ridge-top fog and low cloud in winter cut visibility to 100-300 m and keep drones and helicopters down; summer haze over the coast. Terraces and maquis give constant concealment.
weather.dust_or_snow: Little dust; snow on ridges above 700 m a few days each winter.

civilians.behaviour: Population fluctuates with the fighting: border villages are nearly empty with a few returning families; coastal town and villages north of the Litani are busy and crowded with displaced people. Markets 08:00-14:00, schools out at 14:00, evenings on balconies. On alarms civilians stay in basements and ground floors; displaced families drive north in loaded cars along the coastal highway.
vehicles: farm pickups loaded with produce or furniture
civilians.casualty_risk_notes: Dense towns and inhabited villages make the casualty rule central north of the Litani; peacekeepers are neutral units and also count against the player's reputation if harmed (proposed).

factions_present.where: Maquis ridges, tunnel and bunker complexes, villages north of the Litani and in the hills; rocket and drone teams in orchards; small teams infiltrating the occupied south.
Southern half of the map: hilltop outposts, the border strip, patrol roads and junction checkpoints; drones and air strikes over the whole map (aircraft AI only).
Advisers with hezbollah units only (Quds Force-type), never a field force; appear in HVT and intel contexts.
Border posts at the north-east map edge, anti-smuggling patrols against hezbollah supply routes.
UNIFIL force reserve: armoured patrols on ridge roads, the UN HQ on the coast.

frontline: The south is held by the occupying force and contested by hezbollah teams; the Litani gorge is the de facto line. The war sim moves it in steps: hezbollah attacks on outposts or rocket fire flip ridge zones to contested and trigger occupying-force raids that push north of the Litani for a few days, after which they withdraw to the hilltop line. Ceasefire events freeze the line and post escort, return and UXO contracts instead of combat. UN positions never change hands but shrink over the drawdown: each campaign month removes UN posts, posting evacuation and equipment-escort contracts, until the mandate ends. The contract board here is mostly neutral humanitarian and peacekeeper protection, plus neutral-client isr jobs (drone recovery, infrastructure protection).
contract_hooks: Peacekeeper protection during the drawdown: escort a withdrawing UN convoy through two checkpoints and the Litani bridge (clients aut, irl, ita, fra, esp)
Evacuation of nationals from the coastal town to the harbour and the LHD (clients fra, ita, irl, aut, srb, kaz)
Recover a kidnapped aid worker or peacekeeper from a hill village (client irl or ita)
UXO clearance escort for engineers near UN positions and damaged villages (client irl)
Recover a downed drone from a contested ridge before others reach it (client isr)
Protect a pumping station or power line from rocket teams (client isr, in the south)
Cache survey: locate and document a tunnel and bunker complex for a client (client isr; heavy resistance)
Aid convoy escort to returning families in a damaged border village (neutral clients)

hot_zones.name: Central ridges
hot_zones.layout: hezbollah HQ in a tunnel and bunker complex; 4 outposts in hill villages and maquis; checkpoints on two ridge roads; roaming 2-4 man teams with ATGMs and drones; 1 QRF in a wadi garage; occupying-force outposts on the south edge as a third party

insertion.fob: LHD offshore for most contracts (small boats and helicopters to the harbour or UN HQ helipad). Inland FOB proposed at a UN-shared logistics base north of the Litani; AAVs can land only on the coastal plain, not in the hills.

early_game_notes: hezbollah is mid-tier and Israeli forces are high strength; the escort and evacuation contracts can still be offered early as low-combat jobs.
